_doc: Every tunable assumption in one place. The map, trip planner, demand model and reports all read this file, so they can never drift apart again.

wait._doc: Expected wait = headway / 2, capped (riders time arrivals on long headways). Waits count `weight` times in-vehicle minutes, as riders perceive them (planning practice 2-3x), in routing, the logit and the competitive-commute test.

access._doc: How people reach stations. Walk to anything within walk_max_m; drive (park & ride) to garages within pnr_max_km but not closer than pnr_min_km (people that close walk): commuter rail stations, each line's planned termini, today's lots at existing suburban stations (pnr_existing) and optional suburban garages (pnr_suburban). Garages hold pnr_spaces cars (DART Parker Road ~2,000, TRE/TEXRail stations 175-1,000); each space serves pnr_people_per_space commuters a day (75% full x 1.1 per car x 1.15 with drop-offs). Riders a full garage turns away take their best access without parking (pnr_overflow_fallback). Today's local buses are the feeder grid (30 min in denser areas); faster grids are a lever. Riders choose each station's access mode by perceived minutes (out-of-vehicle time weighs 2.5x). circuity applies to drive access, walk_circuity to walking. The micromobility, kiss_ride and pnr_suburban blocks are levers, off by default.

pnr_suburban._doc: Lever (off by default): a structured garage of `spaces` at selected stations of `modes`, Wiehle-Reston East style (wrapped by development, so TOD uplift is unchanged): only where the station's setting (growth.setting, base-year density) is `setting`, at least min_core_km from a downtown and min_spacing_km from every other garage, outermost first, from from_year. No new parking at downtown or urban stations. Freeway/arterial access is not checked (no road data).

feeder._doc: Lever (off by default): a frequent local bus grid as an access and egress mode. Zones whose activity density (people + jobs per km2 within 800 m) is at least min_density_per_km2 reach any station within max_km (straight line) by bus: stop_walk_min + half the headway (capped like rail waits) + distance x circuity / speed (slowed by road congestion) + transfer_penalty_min. Only the walk, wait and transfer count as out-of-vehicle time. headway_min is a {year: minutes} table, no feeder before its first year. The asc was calibrated without feeders (today's buses sit inside it), so either start the table after 2025 (an upper bound: today's bus-to-rail riders get counted twice) or include today's headway from 2025 and recalibrate (evaluate.calibrate_asc). Bus legs are not rail boardings: run_year reports them separately as feeder_boardings.

micromobility._doc: Lever (off by default): bike / e-scooter access. Only `share` of commuters will ride (a market segment, so it can't turn everyone into a cyclist); they reach stations within max_km at speed_kmh plus penalty_min (unlock, secure parking), and ride on to work if egress.

kiss_ride._doc: Lever (off by default): drop-off or ride-hail to any station, no garage needed. Only `share` of commuters have a driver or will pay for a ride (a market segment); drive at pnr_speed_kmh within max_km, plus penalty_min (curb wait, and the fare expressed as minutes).

pnr_existing._doc: Today's park & ride lots at existing rail stations outside the core (DART has lots at most suburban stations, roughly 100-2,000 spaces each; an approximation until the real inventory is loaded).

congestion._doc: Peak drive times (moving part) grow per_decade from base_year, capped; BRT running time takes brt_share of the increase. TTI travel-time index: about +3% per decade nationally and in DFW. Mild on purpose: congestion forecasts usually overshoot.

competitive._doc: A commute is transit-competitive if transit <= ratio*drive + slack, under the cap, and longer than min_km.

demand._doc: If data/raw/od_tracts.csv (LODES OD aggregated to tracts, see data/README.md) exists it is used directly. Otherwise a doubly-constrained gravity model is synthesized from tract population and jobs, with beta calibrated against the v1 LODES run.

cost_musd_per_km._doc: Capital cost per route-km by mode and grade, 2025 USD. Calibrated to recent US projects: DART Silver Line ~$45M/km (new track on freight ROW), TEXRail ~$24M/km, Houston/Indy BRT $5-25M/km, US light rail $100-200M/km, US subway $400M+/km.

standards._doc: Stop-spacing bands (km) used by validate. Sources in reports/DESIGN_STANDARDS.md.

cores._doc: Downtown cores: proposed metro inside these radii is costed as tunnel.

budget._doc: Flat capital budget (2025 $M per year) with carryover. Spending is spread over each piece's construction years (staging.construction_years). tolerance = share over budget before validation warns.

staging._doc: Rules for staged build-out (dfwt/staging.py, python -m dfwt stage).

geometry._doc: Alignment design limits (dfwt/align.py, python -m dfwt align). Rmin = minimum curve radius (m); Lp = straight platform length (m); tol = how far the fitted alignment may leave the drawn/routed corridor (m) by grade; Ltmin = minimum tangent between curves; jerk/alat govern spiral length; station_move_auto_m = largest station move applied without review. check_radius_m = tightest curve the validator accepts on each mode (commuter trains run on existing freight track, where curves of ~175 m (10 degrees) are common and simply carry a speed limit). straighten_move_max_m = how far a proposed metro station may move onto the direct path between its neighbors to remove a detour (a 10-minute walk). straighten_move_far_m = the same for sharp jogs (60+ degrees). A stop the line would have to double back for (90+ degrees) is dropped from that line.

growth._doc: Zone population and jobs by year (dfwt/growth.py). Multipliers are relative to the base data (2020 population, 2022 jobs) and interpolated between years; the mid case follows NCTCOG Mobility 2050 (12.4M in 2050) and flattens toward 2100 as national growth stalls (Census 2023 projections). low/high are alternatives for scenarios. TOD adds growth within radius_m of stations opened after existing_year (full within full_radius_m), ramping in along a logistic curve (half at ramp_mid_years, width ramp_width_years). Uplift depends on the station's setting (by people+jobs density within 800 m) times a mode factor; net_new_share of it is new to the region and the rest is drawn from elsewhere (rail mostly moves growth around: Cervero & Seskins; NITC station-area studies).

capture._doc: Growth-capture land-use policy (dfwt/growth.capture), off while the shares are 0. From start_year, every step_years: job_centers.jobs_share of the region's job growth goes to the listed job centers (in proportion to the jobs there); then pop_share / jobs_share of the growth that would have landed outside station areas moves into zones within radius_m of open stations (include_existing: today's stations too), up to target_density_per_km2 (people + jobs, by station setting) x mode_factor over each station's own land (overlapping discs split by nearest station). Targets follow the Ontario Growth Plan MTSA minimums (200/ha subway, 160/ha LRT/BRT, 150/ha GO = 20,000/16,000/15,000 per km2) up to Rosslyn-Ballston (about 112 people+jobs per acre = 27,600/km2; Rosslyn 162/acre = 40,000/km2). Within a station area growth is placed by distance (full within full_radius_m) x existing activity. What doesn't fit stays where it was; regional totals never change.

ridership._doc: Daily riders from the commute model (dfwt/demand.py). Each commute chooses drive, transit or walk/bike the whole way (multinomial logit, drive is the reference). Transit utility: asc + b_ivt*(drive - transit door-to-door minutes) - b_ovt_extra*(access + egress minutes) - b_ratio*(how far transit exceeds 1x the drive time, as a ratio) + 0.125/$ x (driving cost avoided at drive_usd_per_km + parking avoided at paid-parking destinations). FTA/MWCOG ranges: IVT -0.02..-0.03/min, out-of-vehicle 2-3x. asc is calibrated so the 2025 network carries today's rail ridership with today's buses as feeders; active.asc so ~2% walk or bike. Transit commuters x telework; daily trips = commuters x round_trip / work_share_of_transit_trips; boardings = trips x boardings per trip (from the load assignment). Drive-to-transit has its own constant (pnr_asc_offset, as in MPO models: parking, walking in from the lot), set so about half of 2025 rail riders drive to a garage, near DART's on-board surveys; riders without a car (no_car) can't.

calibration._doc: DART light rail ~65k weekday + TRE + TEXRail + A-train (APTA/NTD 2024-25). Local buses are not modeled.

paid_parking._doc: Destinations where parking costs money ($/day, approximate).

parking_policy._doc: Parking pricing policy (Zones.parking_usd), off while price_growth is 0 and priced_centers/cashout are null. Phases in linearly from start_year to full_year. price_growth: real rise in paid_parking district prices (fewer free or cheap spaces downtown, e.g. +1.0 = double). priced_centers: wherever jobs within 800 m reach min_jobs_per_km2, parking costs usd_per_day (x the same price growth): paid-parking districts spread as job centers densify. cashout: commuters to other zones with min_jobs_per_km2 are offered usd_per_day in lieu of free parking, at `coverage` of them (California-style parking cash-out; Shoup 1997: drive-alone share 76% -> 63%).

active._doc: Walk/bike the whole way, an alternative in the logit for trips up to max_km: blended speed, effort per minute weighted like out-of-vehicle time, asc calibrated so ~2% of commuters walk or bike (ACS: DFW ~1.5-2%).

no_car._doc: Commuters from households without a car, by the people+jobs density around their home zone (approximate, from ACS: ~5% of DFW households, ~9% in the city of Dallas, 15-25% in dense inner neighborhoods). They can't park & ride; their alternative to transit is getting a ride, which is ride_bonus less attractive than driving yourself.
